topic_scope_candidate: jamming transition in frictionless sphere packings near point J

inclusion_rules.scope_definition: Compile a bounded 1998-2010 packet around the classic point-J route in frictionless sphere packings, while keeping frictional and hard-sphere variants visible as nearby but distinct alternatives.
hard_exclusion_rules: exclude papers published after 2010 from packet inputs
exclude generic granular rheology papers that do not directly constrain point-J or nearby packing routes
exclude later review syntheses from training input even if they summarize the same route
role_assignment_rules: core_method papers must directly build or scale the frictionless point-J route
resource_or_benchmark papers must define a canonical packing reference, protocol, or evaluation frame reused by the route
limitation_or_critique papers must expose instability, protocol dependence, or ambiguity in the baseline point-J picture
alternative_route papers must stay historically visible at the cutoff while remaining meaningfully distinct from the main frictionless route
inclusion_rules.leakage_policy: Papers after the cutoff are excluded from packet input. Later reviews and retrospective syntheses are audit-only, never training input. Hindsight labels and post-cutoff judgments cannot be used in packet compilation.

included_items.inclusion_reason: Provides the early jamming-diagram and fragile-matter framing that defines the packet's conceptual boundary before the point-J line is formalized.
included_items.title: Jamming, Force Chains, and Fragile Matter

included_items.inclusion_reason: Supplies the maximally-random-jammed framing and compression-protocol reference point used as a canonical benchmark for random packing claims.
included_items.title: Is Random Close Packing of Spheres Well Defined?

included_items.inclusion_reason: Introduces the numerical route around random packings of frictionless particles and ties the packing threshold to the jamming threshold.
included_items.title: Random Packings of Frictionless Particles

included_items.inclusion_reason: Stabilizes point J as the main frictionless route by explicitly grounding jamming at zero temperature and zero applied stress.
included_items.title: Jamming at zero temperature and zero applied stress: The epitome of disorder

included_items.inclusion_reason: Adds linear-response critical scaling and thus strengthens the route's quantitative readout near the jamming transition.
included_items.title: Critical Scaling in Linear Response of Frictionless Granular Packings near Jamming

included_items.inclusion_reason: Keeps the frictional-sphere route visible as a nearby alternative so replay can compare the main frictionless route against a historically real competing path.
included_items.title: Jamming of frictional spheres and random loose packing

included_items.inclusion_reason: Explicitly challenges the idea of a single universal jamming density and therefore acts as the packet's main critique / stability check.
included_items.title: Jamming Transitions in Amorphous Packings of Frictionless Spheres Occur over a Continuous Range of Volume Fractions

excluded_items.notes: Quasistatic shear-flow probe paper is relevant but not historically visible at the 2010 cutoff.
Finite-system synthesis is useful for audit but beyond the pilot cutoff.
Later hard-sphere equilibrium sampling result is audit-only for this packet.
Later review is useful for retrospective audit but cannot enter packet input.
Deep-learning jamming analogy is outside the physical granular route for this pilot.
